title: Compatible compactification towers with a supplied compactification of the composite
statement: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be separated finite-type morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with separatedness and finite type as in [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose given compactifications $d=(i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y,q:\overline Y\to Z)$ of $h$ and $c=(a_0:X\hookrightarrow W,t:W\to Z)$ of $hf$, meaning quasi-compact open first maps [def-weil-open-immersion] and proper second maps [def-weil-proper-morphism]. There exists a compactification $e=(a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to\overline Y)$ of $if$ and a proper map $v:\overline X\to W$ with $va=a_0$ and $tv=qp$. Put $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $b:U\to\overline X$ and $p_Y:U\to Y$. Then $b$ and the induced $c_X:X\to U$ are quasi-compact open immersions, $p_Y$ is proper, $bc_X=a$ and $p_Yc_X=f$. Thus $(c_X,p_Y)$ compactifies $f$, $(a,qp)$ compactifies $hf$, and $p b=i p_Y$ is cartesian. These data base-change to a tower of the same kind under any map $Z'\to Z$. Any two such towers for $f,h$ admit a common refining tower, with compatible proper maps on their ambient compactifications and on their intermediate schemes $U$, commuting with all tower arrows and restricting to the identity on $X,Y$. In particular, a refining tower indexed by $1$ mapping to a tower indexed by $2$ has proper maps $v$ on the ambient compactifications of $X$, $u$ on the ambient compactifications of $Y$, and $w:U_1\to U_2$, with $va_1=a_2$, $ui_1=i_2$, $wc_1=c_2$, $vb_1=b_2w$, $p_2v=up_1$, $p_{Y,2}w=p_{Y,1}$ and $q_2u=q_1$; here $c_1,c_2$ denote the open maps from $X$ to the intermediate schemes. No qcqs hypothesis is imposed on $Z$; existence of the displayed compactifications is part of the data.

proof.text: Form $P=W\times_Z\overline Y$ and $r=(a_0,if):X\to P$. The equality $ta_0=hf=qif$ gives this map. Both projections of $P$ are proper by base change; in particular they are separated. Since $\operatorname{pr}_W r=a_0$ is a quasi-compact open immersion (hence an immersion, using the identity closed immersion in its factorization), cancellation shows that $r$ is a quasi-compact immersion.

proof.text: Apply the immersion-compactification construction to $r$ over $\overline Y$: put $\overline X=\operatorname{SIm}(r)$, write $k:\overline X\hookrightarrow P$ for its closed inclusion, and $a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ for the image factor, so $ka=r$. This gives a compactification of $if$, with $p=\operatorname{pr}_{\overline Y}k$ proper and $a$ a quasi-compact open immersion. Put $v=\operatorname{pr}_W k$. A closed immersion followed by a proper map is proper, so $v$ is proper. Projection identities give $va=a_0$, $pa=if$, and $tv=qp$. Composition of proper maps makes $qp$ proper, so $(a,qp)$ compactifies $hf$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition; first paragraph and its top ambient compactification; supplied-compactification graph construction as in WeilConjectures/Compactification/Comp.lean and Triangle.lean

proof.text: Put $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$. The projection $b$ is a quasi-compact open immersion by base change of $i$, and $p_Y$ is proper by base change of $p$. The pair $(a,f)$ gives $c_X:X\to U$. To check that $c_X$ is the base change of $a$ along $b$, let $x:T\to X$ and $u:T\to U$ satisfy $ax=bu$. Write $y=p_Yu$. Then $iy=pbu=pax=ifx$. Since an open immersion identifies its domain with an open subscheme, $i$ is a monomorphism, so $y=fx$. The two projections of $u$ are therefore $ax,fx$, and fibre-product uniqueness gives $u=c_Xx$. Conversely $bc_Xx=ax$, so this constructs the inverse to the projection $U\times_{\overline X}X\to X$. Thus $c_X$ is a base change of the quasi-compact open immersion $a$, and the cited openness and quasi-compactness base-change lemmas give both properties directly. The projection equations are $bc_X=a$, $p_Yc_X=f$, and $pb=ip_Y$. This proves the required restriction compactification and cartesian square.

proof.text: For any $Z'\to Z$, pull back every displayed scheme and arrow over $Z$. The base-changed maps $f'$ and $h'$ remain separated and of finite type by the cited stability node, applied along $Y\times_Z Z'\to Y$ and $Z'\to Z$ respectively. Properness, openness and quasi-compactness of the designated maps survive by their respective base-change lemmas. The universal property of fibre products identifies $U\times_Z Z'$ with $(\overline X\times_Z Z')\times_{\overline Y\times_Z Z'}(Y\times_Z Z')$. Projection identities and $ka=r$ pull back to the same identities, so the pulled-back data form a tower with the pulled-back supplied compactifications. This asserts stability of the data, not that forming the scheme-theoretic image commutes with arbitrary base change.

proof.text: Now take two towers, writing their ambient schemes as $A_j=\overline X_j$ and $B_j=\overline Y_j$, with $p_j:A_j\to B_j$ and $q_j:B_j\to Z$. Apply cofilteredness for the compactifiable separated finite-type map $h:Y\to Z$ to its two supplied objects $(i_j,q_j)$. It gives a compactification $j:Y\hookrightarrow D$, $q:D\to Z$ and proper maps $u_j:D\to B_j$ with $u_jj=i_j$ and $q_ju_j=q$. This invocation uses no qcqs hypothesis on $Z$.

proof.text: Form $P_j=A_j\times_{B_j}D$ and $P=P_1\times_D P_2$. Each $P_j\to D$ is proper by base change of $p_j$, so $P\to D$ is proper by base change and composition, and $P\to Z$ is proper. The projections $P\to A_j$ are $Z$-maps into schemes separated over $Z$ (since $q_jp_j$ is proper), hence are proper. Define $r:X\to P$ using the pairs $(a_j,jf)$: the equations $p_ja_j=i_jf=u_jjf$ and equality of their $D$-components give the lift. Its composite with $P\to A_1$ is $a_1$, a quasi-compact immersion; cancellation therefore makes $r$ a quasi-compact immersion. The immersion construction over $D$ gives $a:X\hookrightarrow A=\operatorname{SIm}(r)$ and a proper $p:A\to D$. The restricted projections $v_j:A\to A_j$ are proper because the image inclusion is closed and $P\to A_j$ is proper. By the projection identities, $v_ja=a_j$, $p_jv_j=u_jp$ and $q_j u_j=q$.

proof.text: Use step 3 for $(a,p,j)$ to obtain the intermediate scheme $U=A\times_DY$, its quasi-compact open maps $c:X\to U$, $b:U\to A$, and the proper map $p_Y:U\to Y$. For each $j$, define $w_j:U\to U_j=A_j\times_{B_j}Y$ by the pair $(v_jb,p_Y)$. The needed equation is $p_jv_jb=u_jpb=u_jjp_Y=i_jp_Y$. Thus $b_jw_j=v_jb$ and $p_{Y,j}w_j=p_Y$. Since $U\to Y$ is proper and $U_j\to Y$ is proper, hence separated, $w_j$ is proper. On $X$, the two components of $w_jc$ are $v_ja=a_j$ and $f$, which are exactly those of $c_j$; fibre-product uniqueness gives $w_jc=c_j$. Together with the equations in step 6 these are every required compatibility, restricting to the identity on $X,Y$. Relabel a refining tower and a target tower by 1 and 2 to obtain precisely the seven equations in the statement.
